review_notes: I read the whole file. It has no `@[simp]` lemmas. The only simp-adjacent attributes are `gcongr` and `mono` on the monotonicity lemmas, and those look correct. I checked the iff lemmas that could plausibly be simp lemmas: `hasProd_one_iff`, `hasProd_one_iff_of_one_le`, `Multipliable.tprod_eq_one_iff`, `Multipliable.tprod_ne_one_iff`, `multipliable_mabs_iff` and the `summable_abs_iff` aliases. Each needs side conditions (`Multipliable`, `LeAtTop`, `NeBot`, or non-negativity), and I found no concrete uses in Mathlib that would be better served by a simp attribute. For example, `ENNReal.lean` and `ZetaValues.lean` call `tsum_eq_zero_iff` and `summable_abs_iff` explicitly through `rw`. Adding a simp attribute to those lemmas would be speculative. I found no competing rules, unwanted expansion or credible rewrite cycles. The positivity extension is not part of the simp interface. I did not run Lean, and I only grepped for uses rather than reading every one.
